newsitem.title: UK: Swedish bonds seen forging on despite EMU stance.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bonds seen forging on despite EMU stance.

text.p: Swedish bonds will prosper as the market looks on the bright side of Sweden's decision not to join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) at the 1999 start date, analysts said on Tuesday. Even though Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said the country would not join, analysts gleaned positive sign from some of his comments, notably that the door to EMU had not be closed completely.
"No in 1999 was expected," said Stephanie Pfeifer, European economist at Deustche Morgan Grenfell. "I do not think it will have much effect at all on the bond market."
Persson also said Sweden would join EMU when possible and that he sought to send a positive signal on EMU.
"This is more positive than expected," said Pfeifer.
The 10-year Swedish bond was quoted at 107.44 at 1520 GMT, and the spread against 10-year Bunds widened one basis point to 111 basis points.

"Developments in Europe over the last couple of weeks have pointed to a softer euro, so the price of staying out of EMU is getting lower and lower," Jan Haggstrom, chief financial officer at Handelsbanken in Stockholm, told Reuters Financial Television.
There would be further convergence between Swedish and German bonds, Haggstrom added.
Sweden's Persson also said a decision about Sweden joining EMU would be made only after some type of poll.
But conversely, EMU friendly comments by Sweden could have an adverse effect on its bond markets, some economists said.
"Sweden has been benefiting from its safe haven status because it has distanced itself from EMU," said David Brown, chief European economist at Bear Stearns International in London.
